For whom did she bear, if it is not true that she bore Emmanuel according to the flesh? Let those, then, be laughed at who babble these and such things about me. For holy Isaiah does not lie when he prophesies thus: Behold, a virgin shall conceive in the womb and bear a son, and they shall call him Emmanuel, which is, God with us (Isa. 7). And beyond doubt Gabriel the archangel spoke truly when he addressed Mary thus: Do not fear, Mary, for you have found favour with God. Behold, you will conceive in the womb and bear a son, and you will call his name Jesus; for he will save his people from their sins (Luke 1; Matt. 1). And when we say that our Lord Jesus Christ came down from heaven above, we do not say it in the sense that we think he brought his holy flesh down from heaven; but we follow holy Paul, who says thus: The first man was from the earth, earthly; the second, the Lord from heaven (1 Cor. 15). We imitate also the Lord himself, who says: No one has ascended into heaven except he who descended from heaven, the Son of Man (John 3). But as regards the flesh, he was born, as we have said, of the blessed Virgin. But since the Word of God, descending from heaven, emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, and became son of man, while yet remaining the same as he was before, namely God (for he is immutable, and of a nature subject to no alteration), since he is now understood to be one with his own flesh, he is said to have come from heaven. And he is also called man from heaven, since he is perfect in deity and the same perfect in humanity, and is understood to be one person. For the Lord Jesus Christ is one, even though the difference of the natures is not unknown, from which we say that ineffable union was made. We confess, therefore, that the Word, the Only-begotten Son of God, is perfect God and perfect man, consisting of a body and a soul endowed with reason; as regards the deity, born of the Father before the ages, and the same in the last times, for us and for our salvation, of the Virgin Mary according to the humanity; consubstantial with the Father according to the divinity, and consubstantial with us according to the humanity. For a union of two natures has been made. Hence it is that we confess one Christ, one Son, one Lord, and also that the holy Virgin was truly Mother of God, because God the Word put on flesh and became man, and in the very conception united to himself the temple which he was taking from her. If you please, let us take as an example our own composition, insofar as we are men. We consist, of course, of soul and body. And we see two natures, one of the body, another of the soul; but the man, made from the union of both, is one; nor does the composition from two natures make us think of two men instead of one, but we understand (as I said) one man composed of soul and body. For if we take this away, that from two different natures one undivided Christ exists from the union, the adversaries will say: If there is one nature of the whole Christ, how could he put on human nature, or adopt flesh as his own? And may your piety deign openly to stop the mouths of those who say that a tempering together, confusion or mixture of the natures of the Word of God with the flesh took place." After this, when Cyril had died, there emerged a certain monk and archimandrite named Eutyches. He attached to himself no small part of the people, approving the sect of Nestorius and his impious doctrine, and saying that the Lord's flesh is not consubstantial with us. And again not long afterwards, the devil's hand prevailing, another council at Ephesus, of robbers and by no means holy, was assembled, Flavian of Constantinople also being sent to it, while the supreme control of affairs there lay with Dioscorus, bishop of Alexandria. The divine Flavian, defending the orthodox faith, was killed; and the authority of the first synod of Ephesus was abrogated, certain bishops subscribing under compulsion of deadly force, among whom was also Basil, bishop of Seleucia. Hence, since the pernicious doctrines of Nestorius, Dioscorus and Eutyches were being taught publicly, and great tumults arose especially in the East, Proterius, the great priest, and very many others were killed. In this state of affairs Marcian was by divine providence made emperor; he assembled at Chalcedon a council of six hundred and thirty Fathers, in the presence of Dioscorus and Eutyches, and himself attended it together with them; and there Dioscorus and Eutyches were condemned, and Nestorius was anathematised again; Theodoret likewise, Ibas, and Basil, bishop of Seleucia, were received, although they had previously subscribed to the council. And so, the acts of the robber synod having been abolished and condemned, concord among all was brought about by the holy Fathers. These four councils having thus been held and confirmed, and holding authority in the Church of God, the followers of Nestorius once more confirmed their heresy by means of the works of Theodore of Mopsuestia, who blasphemed far worse things than Nestorius his disciple. We, therefore, following our holy fathers, and wishing to preserve the right faith without any stain, exhort you to examine his blasphemies too and to pass sentence on him [and] his followers. For besides countless other curses which he impiously vomited out against Christ our God, he also put forward this: that God the Word is one, and Christ another, who, troubled by passions of the soul and desires of the flesh, gradually withdrew from what is worse, and by progress in deeds turned out better, and followed a blameless manner of the best life; who, as a mere man, baptised in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, obtained through baptism the grace of the Holy Spirit and was deemed worthy of adoption; and, in the manner of a royal image, Christ was worshipped in the person of God the Word, and after the resurrection was of a steadfast mind, free of sins. Furthermore he declared that the union of the Word with Christ was such as the Apostle spoke of between man and woman: And the two shall be in one flesh. To this I exhort you also to examine the things wickedly written by Theodoret and Ibas against the first holy council of Ephesus, and to pass sentence against them in the same way.

The fathers, having again considered these things carefully, replied: The holy council of Chalcedon, after sharply attacking Theodoret and Ibas in words, received them back into favour on no other condition than that they should first condemn their own wicked writings, and Theodore and Nestorius. But we, besides all the other heretics condemned by the said four holy councils and excluded from the Church, also condemn and proscribe Theodore, who was bishop of Mopsuestia, and his impious books; and also the things which Theodoret wrote wickedly against the true faith, and against the twelve chapters of St Cyril, and the first holy synod of Ephesus, and in defence of Theodore and Nestorius. Furthermore we also condemn the letter which Ibas is said to have written to Maris the Persian, which denies that the Word of God, incarnate of the holy Virgin Mary, Mother of God, was made man, and denounces the divine Cyril as a heretic; and it censures the first holy synod of Ephesus, as having condemned Nestorius without examining the case; and it spits upon the twelve chapters of St Cyril, while it champions Nestorius and Theodore and their impious writings and opinions. Therefore, rightly reckoning the unbridled tongues of these heretics, and their most impious writings, and the men themselves, persevering to the end in their false opinions and malice, among [the portion of] the devil, the father of lies, we shall say: Go in the light of your fire, and in the flame which you have kindled.
